messages.subject: Setting up project with transects used multiple times
parts:
Hi all,
I would be very grateful for some advice on setting up my data in Distanc=
e. I have done 4 counts (2 summer, 2 winter over 1 yr) of bustards on a t=
otal of about 4500 km of roads in South Africa. I realise the issues with=
using roads, but I am repeating the methodology of surveys done exactly =
this way in the 1980s (the routes only differ in the current surveys slig=
htly where roads became impassable in places etc), and I have some satell=
ite tracking data which I am hoping will support my theory that these bir=
ds do not avoid roads. The route is mostly continuous, and goes through 1=
8 different bioregions. In the 1980s, 4 surveys were done, but distance m=
easurements were only made on 1 survey. There is a strong seasonal effect=
(lots of birds in winter, not in summer), so I will focus on winter coun=
ts.
The overall aims of the research are to see if there has been a populatio=
n decline and to estimate a current population (which I was planning to d=
o stratified by bioregion). So I have set up my project using bioregion a=
s region, the 5 surveys (4 of mine and 1 historic) as line transects (the=
amount of road travelled in each bioregion), and then the sighting data =
as observations. Using the data filters I am planning to come up with an =
density for just the historic survey, and then a current one (using my wi=
nter data).
I am just a bit concerned that the line transects in each season are the =
same and not independent, so I wondered if I have set this up in the appr=
opriate way? I looked at multipliers but I don't think I can use these an=
d still keep the season data?
Many thanks
Jessica

ratified by bioregion). So I have set up my project using bioregion as regi=
on, the 5 surveys (4 of mine and 1 historic) as line transects (the amount =
of road travelled in each bioregion), and then the sighting data as observa=
tions. Using the data filters I am planning to come up with an density for =
just the historic survey, and then a current one (using my winter data).
I am just a bit concerned that the line transects in each season are the sa=

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: Setting up project with transects used multiple times
parts:
Pablo-

If you visited the transect 4 times, you should enter each transect as a
single sample record and the value of the effort should be 4 times the
length of the transect, if this is line transect data. If it is point data
then the effort should be entered as 4 for each point. Unless you misstated
the comparison of old and new below, this will not help resolve the
differences because this will reduce the density of your current survey if
you entered the sightings from all 4 visits but only entered the effort as
1 times the length of the line.

--jeff
